subject: On-prem streaming acceptance runbook and network handoff
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anne Li <anne.li@vectorhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem streaming acceptance runbook and network handoff

Hi Anne — great call earlier, thanks for the time. Quick written recap and an initial acceptance/runbook draft so your networking team has something to act on. I pulled in Karthik (networking/ops) and Neha (solutions) so they can own the technical checks.

Summary from the call:
- Goal: validate on-prem/VPC path for low-latency streaming inference (SSE/websocket) for an initial POC (3-day window).
- Target SLAs we discussed: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 80ms, p99 tail < 150ms for single-stream responses when routed through the private connector. For streaming (tokenized chunking) we capped tail budget at 200ms per chunk.
- Throughput expectation for POC: sustained 400 RPS aggregate, with 150 concurrent streaming sessions (average 2 concurrent streams per user).
- Fallback: Redwood will provide an HTTP/gRPC fallback to the hosted cluster if the private path exceeds 500ms for >5% of requests over a 5m window.

Immediate network handoff checklist (actionable items for VectorHealth networking):
1) Peering vs. VPN: you indicated preference for VPN (IPSec) for initial POC. Please confirm whether you want IPsec site-to-site or a managed VPN tunnel. If you can support AWS/GCP/Azure VPC peering, that is preferred for lower jitter — call it option B.
2) IP ranges: provide the source CIDR(s) that will originate inference traffic from your on‑prem cluster to Redwood egress points.
3) Ports/Protocols: allow outbound TCP 443 and UDP 1194/500/4500 (if you opt for UDP-based tunnel). Also whitelist our egress IP block: 54.210.33.0/24 (example; we'll provide the exact set in the runbook).
4) Baseline measurements we need from your team: 3 runs of iperf3 between your edge gateway and our egress IP; 5-minute packet captures during a demo stream; and tracert/mtr to the three Redwood edge nodes listed in the Drive doc.
5) Jitter/Packet loss thresholds: target jitter < 10ms, packet loss < 0.1% for sustained windows; intermittent spikes are OK if transient under 30s.

Acceptance criteria (POC gating):
- Functional: streaming tokens delivered in-order with no corruption, streaming reconnect within 3s for transient path failovers.
- Performance: p95 < 80ms and p99 < 150ms for single-user streams during a 15m sustained load test at 150 concurrent streams.
- Throughput: aggregate 400 RPS sustained for 10 minutes with <1% error rate.
- Operational: shared logging (sflow/pcap samples) and traced request ids attached to Redwood Console traces within 24h of test.

Attachments included: slo-matrix.xlsx (detailed numerical targets), network-trace-sample.txt (example traceroutes), redwood-poc-runbook.pdf (step-by-step environment setup).

Next steps / owners:
- VectorHealth networking: run iperf3/traceroute and drop results in the Drive folder; confirm whether peering is supported or VPN only (owner: Anne) — target 2028-07-26 EOD.
- Redwood ops: pre-create private connector and reserve a 3-node POC pool; share exact egress IPs and test endpoints (owner: Karthik) — target 2028-07-26 EOD.
- Security/Procurement: we hear Procurement will need a short questionnaire; happy to fill and return (owner: Neha) — target 2028-07-28.

If anything above is off from what your team expects, flag it and we'll update the runbook. If this looks good, can we lock a POC window next Tue–Thu (July 31–Aug 2)?

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Anne Li <anne.li@vectorhealth.com>

- Our edge NAT will rewrite source IPs; does Redwood require preserved source addressing for per-customer routing?

I'll confirm Procurement timeline separately (they're CC'd). POC window July 31–Aug 2 looks fine from our side; please send a calendar invite.

—Anne

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem streaming acceptance runbook and network handoff

Hi Anne — quick technical notes from our operations side after reviewing your note about NAT and site-to-site VPNs.

1) NAT / Source IPs: we can support a NATed source (session affinity by session token) but if you want per-customer routing to an isolated private connector we need either preserved source or SNI-based routing + auth header. For the POC it's OK to proceed with NATed source; we will rely on a signed customer token for affinity.

2) Tests we will run from Redwood during the POC:
   - Controlled synthetic streams to each session to verify chunk RTT and reorder tolerance.
   - Concurrent ramp: ramp to 150 concurrent streams over 300s and hold for 10 minutes.
   - Burst test: generate a 2x traffic burst for 60s to validate autoscaling/fallback.

3) Measurement tooling & traces: please include an example request id header (x-rw-request-id) when you run iperf/traceroute if possible — it helps correlate logs. If not, we'll assign per-test ids on our side and map by timestamps.

4) Acceptance note regarding egress: if using VPN, plan for an extra 10–25ms added tail latency; we'll bake that into the acceptance for VPN option A. If peering becomes available we can reduce the tail budget.

I'll upload a short runbook snippet to the Drive (network-checklist.md) and share the edge IP list by EOD.

—Karthik
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anne Li <anne.li@vectorhealth.com>, netstream-eng@vectorhealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem streaming acceptance runbook and network handoff

Thanks all — short update and pinned next steps now that we have confirmation on VPN: 

- Anne: appreciate the VPN confirmation. For the NATed source, Karthik's plan to use signed tokens for affinity is acceptable for the POC.
- Action: VectorHealth networking to drop iperf/traceroute outputs in the Drive folder and add an example request header if possible. (owner: Anne) — due 2028-07-26 EOD (received).
- Redwood: we created the POC cluster and uploaded edge IPs and network-checklist.md to the Drive folder. Karthik uploaded the edge IPs (see redwood-poc-runbook.pdf).
- Procurement: Neha will work with your Procurement contact to complete the one-page data handling questionnaire (owner: Neha) — target 2028-07-28.
- Calendar invite: provisional POC window Jul 31–Aug 2; I just sent invites to Anne + eng/ops list.

POC acceptance notes (short):
- If during the 10-minute sustained run we exceed p99 > 200ms for >2 consecutive 1-minute buckets, we will mark the trial tactical-fail and run a joint debug session.
- Autoscale/fallback: Redwood will enable a soft fallback to hosted endpoints if the VPN path shows >5% errors over a rolling 5m window.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC. Will follow up the minute we have your iperf outputs.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
